channel.title: Natural Health News UK - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Natural Health News UK (naturalhealthnews.uk)

item.title: Edible flowers could help boost vitamin E intake
item.description: Edible flowers are a surprising source of healthy fatty-acids, carotenoids and more, according to new research.

item.title: Vitamin D status linked to Parkinson’s symptoms
item.description: New evidence suggests that low vitamin D status plays an important role in the development of Parkinson's Disease and a corresponding increase in the frequency of falls and insomnia.

item.title: Stay positive, live longer
item.description: Optimism - the ability to see the glass half full rather than half empty - could be the key to a longer life for both men and women.

item.title: Do tea drinkers have better organised brains?
item.description: That tea break could be doing more than just giving you an injection of caffeine - it could help protect against age-related decline in the way the brain organises information.

item.title: Study finds cancer-causing contaminants in US tap water
item.description: US data finds naturally occurring arsenic, the byproducts of chemicals used to disinfect water and radioactive elements top the list of tap water contaminants.

item.title: New evidence shows gut bacteria work in teams
item.description: New research shows that teamwork is key for the trillions of bacteria that live in our gut and this has a big impact on our overall health and well-being.

item.title: Taking vitamin D by oral spray just as effective as taking a tablet
item.description: Taking vitamin D by oral spray is just as effective as taking a tablet, and many find sprays easier to take and more convenient.

item.title: High fibre, yogurt consumption could help lower lung cancer risk
item.description: The prebiotic/probiotic combination found in yogurt and high fibre foods could strengthen the microbiome and help protect against lung cancer, say scientists.

item.title: Sunscreen chemicals enter bloodstream after a single application
item.description: After just one application of sunscreen, a range of worrying chemicals can be absorbed into the bloodstream at levels that exceed official safety thresholds.

item.title: UK supermarkets still supporting deforestation soya
item.description: Soya in the meat and dairy supply chains of UK supermarkets could be contributing to illegal deforestation in the Amazon undermining customer-friendly claims of a 'clean' soya supply chain.
